LESSON: DRAWING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.3: Drawing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Drawing, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do lines appear in the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Drawing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: as the learner draws different lines and create texture on the drawn shapes,

• Communication: as the learner speaks clearly, mentioning lines found in the environment.

Values:
• Unity is promoted as the learner cooperatively works with others in making pattern formations.

• Responsibility is nurtured as the learner cares for resources as they source appropriate materials for drawing such as

coloured pencils, crayons, charcoal

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Health promotion is enhanced as the learner observes hygiene by properly washing hands after rubbing to simulate texture on

found objects in the environment.

Link to other learning areas:

• Mathematical Activities as the learner applies the line drawing skills acquired in Mathematics to draw various lines in the

environment.

• Environmental Activities as the learner names various lines in their environment.

10

Suggested learning resources:

Coloured pencils, crayons, drawing paper, drawing books, books, tablets, text books, plasticine, assistive technology, and

adapted digital devices.
